title: Intensifying adverbs
about: Stronger ways of saying very or very much, and the words each adverb goes with: highly unlikely, utterly ridiculous, bitterly disappointed, deeply ashamed, ridiculously cheap, strongly object. Other combinations, like highly ridiculous or strongly disappointed, sound wrong.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Very, really і extremely підходять майже до всіх звичайних прикметників (very tired, really cold), тому вони рідко бувають помилкою. А кожен підсилювач цього юніту має своїх «партнерів». Absolutely та utterly — тільки з «крайніми» словами (exhausted, ridiculous, impossible, devastated), і з ними very не кажуть. Highly — з likely, successful, recommended; bitterly — з розчаруванням, жалем, образою; deeply — з почуттями; ridiculously — з цінами, розмірами, часом; strongly — з дієсловами думки (believe, recommend, object). Українське «сильно» щоразу перекладаємо по-різному, а strongly ставимо переважно перед дієсловами.

items.pattern: highly (un)likely · It's highly unlikely that… · sb is highly unlikely to…
items.meaning: almost certainly not going to happen (or almost certainly going to happen)
items.example: With all this traffic, it's **highly unlikely** we'll get there by six.
more: It's **highly likely** that the shops will be packed on Saturday.
Rain is **highly unlikely** this week, so you can leave your umbrella at home.
items.watchOut: Не strongly unlikely: strongly ставимо перед дієсловами думки (believe, recommend). З likely / unlikely — highly або very.

items.pattern: highly unusual · It's highly unusual for sb to…
items.meaning: very strange or rare; not what normally happens
items.example: It's **highly unusual** for my dad to forget my birthday.
more: We've had a **highly unusual** amount of snow for April.
The doctor said this kind of rash is **highly unusual** in adults.

items.pattern: highly successful · a highly successful business / career / film
items.meaning: doing very well; getting very good results
items.example: My aunt runs a **highly successful** bakery in the town centre.
more: Our first holiday as a family of five was **highly successful**: nobody got lost and nobody cried.
He had a **highly successful** career as a football coach.
items.watchOut: Successful — прикметник, success — іменник: The party was a big success, але The party was highly successful.

items.pattern: highly profitable · a highly profitable business / shop
items.meaning: making a lot of money
items.example: The little café turned out to be **highly profitable**, so the owners opened a second one.
more: Renting out the spare room to students has been **highly profitable**.
Selling Christmas trees is **highly profitable**, but only for one month a year.

items.pattern: highly competitive · a highly competitive market / job / sport · (of a person) loves to win
items.meaning: with a lot of people trying hard to win or to get the same thing
items.uk: з дуже великою конкуренцією; дуже азартний (про людину)
items.example: Professional football is **highly competitive**, and only a few players make it to the top.
more: Supermarkets keep their prices low because the market is **highly competitive**.
Getting a summer job in our town is **highly competitive**: every café gets dozens of applications.
items.watchOut: Competitive prices — вигідні (конкурентні) ціни. Про людину: she's highly competitive — вона дуже любить вигравати.

items.pattern: highly effective · a highly effective treatment / way to…
items.meaning: working very well; giving the result you want
items.example: This cream is **highly effective** against mosquito bites.
more: A short walk after lunch is a **highly effective** way to stay awake at work.
The new flu vaccine has proved **highly effective**.
items.watchOut: Effective — дієвий, що дає результат. Efficient — економний, продуктивний: a highly efficient dishwasher (витрачає мало води й енергії).

items.pattern: highly controversial · also deeply controversial
items.meaning: causing a lot of disagreement and strong feelings
items.example: The plan to close the village school is **highly controversial**.
more: The referee's decision in the last minute was **highly controversial**.
Building a car park in the old park is a **highly controversial** idea.
items.watchOut: Highly зазвичай іде з позитивними словами, але highly controversial — виняток. Суперечливий (викликає суперечки) — controversial, а не contradictory (той, що сам собі суперечить).

items.pattern: highly recommended · come highly recommended · highly recommend sth
items.meaning: praised a lot by people who have tried it
items.example: The new Thai restaurant on our street comes **highly recommended**.
more: I **highly recommend** this dentist: she's very gentle.
The guided tour of the castle is **highly recommended**, especially for children.
items.watchOut: Не extremely recommended і не very recommended. Highly recommended — дуже хвалять; strongly recommended — наполегливо радять: Booking is strongly recommended.

items.pattern: utterly / absolutely ridiculous
items.meaning: completely silly and unreasonable
items.example: Paying ten pounds for an hour's parking is **utterly ridiculous**.
more: You look **absolutely ridiculous** in that hat!
The rule that kids can't play football in the park is **utterly ridiculous**.
items.watchOut: Ridiculous — уже «крайнє» слово, тому absolutely / utterly ridiculous, а не very чи highly ridiculous. І це «безглуздий, абсурдний», а не просто «смішний» (funny).

items.pattern: absolutely / utterly stupid · an absolutely stupid idea / thing to do
items.meaning: completely silly; showing no good sense
items.example: Leaving the back door open all night was an **absolutely stupid** thing to do.
more: I felt **utterly stupid** when I got on the wrong train.
It's an **absolutely stupid** idea to drive in this snow.

items.pattern: absolutely / utterly impossible · It's absolutely impossible to…
items.meaning: cannot happen or be done at all
items.example: It's **absolutely impossible** to find a parking space here on Saturdays.
more: With two small kids, getting a full night's sleep is **utterly impossible**.
The instructions were only in Japanese, so it was **absolutely impossible** to follow them.
items.watchOut: Не very impossible: щось або можливо, або ні. Кажемо absolutely / completely impossible, а «майже неможливо» — almost / nearly impossible.

items.pattern: absolutely / utterly wrong · You're absolutely wrong
items.meaning: completely not correct
items.example: I was **absolutely wrong** about the new neighbours: they're lovely.
more: You're **absolutely wrong** if you think it's warm in Scotland in May.
The address on the parcel was **utterly wrong**, so it came back to us.
items.watchOut: «Ти помиляєшся» — You're wrong, а не You're not right. Підсилюємо: You're absolutely wrong; протилежне — absolutely right.

items.pattern: utterly / absolutely alone · feel / be utterly alone
items.meaning: completely alone, often feeling that nobody can help you
items.example: In my first month in London I felt **utterly alone**.
more: After her husband died, she was **utterly alone** in that big house.
Lost in the forest at night, the boy felt **absolutely alone**.
items.watchOut: Alone — без людей поруч; lonely — самотній, коли від цього сумно. Utterly alone часто означає і те, й інше.

items.pattern: utterly / absolutely appalled · appalled by / at sth
items.meaning: extremely shocked and upset by something bad
items.example: We were **utterly appalled** by the state of the hotel room.
more: My mum was **absolutely appalled** when she saw the price of the taxi.
Many parents were **utterly appalled** at the food in the school canteen.
items.watchOut: Appalled — обурений і шокований: appalled by / at sth. Не плутай з appealed (звернувся, сподобався).

items.pattern: absolutely / utterly convinced · convinced that… / of sth
items.meaning: completely sure that something is true
items.example: My son is **absolutely convinced** there's a monster under his bed.
more: I'm **utterly convinced** I locked the door, but let's check anyway.
Are you **absolutely convinced** that this is the right bus?
items.watchOut: Переконаний у чомусь — convinced of sth або convinced that…, а не convinced in.

items.pattern: utterly / absolutely devastated · devastated by sth
items.meaning: extremely shocked and sad (a person) or completely destroyed (a place)
items.example: She was **utterly devastated** when her old dog died.
more: Our garden looked **utterly devastated** after the hailstorm.
We were **absolutely devastated** when the wedding venue cancelled our booking a week before the big day.
items.watchOut: Про людину — «вбитий горем, розбитий»: I was devastated, а не I was destroyed.

items.pattern: utterly / absolutely miserable · feel / look utterly miserable
items.meaning: extremely unhappy; also very unpleasant (a day, the weather)
items.uk: зовсім нещасний; жахливий, мерзенний (про день, погоду)
items.example: The kids were **utterly miserable** on the long drive to Grandma's.
more: He looked **absolutely miserable** sitting alone at the bus stop.
It was an **utterly miserable** day: cold, wet and windy.
items.watchOut: Miserable — не «мізерний» (мізерний — tiny, meagre). Miserable — нещасний, жалюгідний; miserable weather — мерзенна погода.

items.pattern: absolutely / utterly exhausted · but very tired
items.meaning: extremely tired, with no energy left
items.example: After the twelve-hour flight we were **absolutely exhausted**.
more: I'm **utterly exhausted**: I've been on my feet all day.
The kids were **absolutely exhausted** after their swimming lesson.
items.watchOut: Very tired, але absolutely exhausted. Absolutely / utterly — з «крайніми» словами (exhausted, starving, freezing), very — зі звичайними (tired, hungry, cold). h у exhausted не вимовляється.

items.pattern: bitterly disappointed (with sth / that… / not to…) · bitterly disappointing · also deeply disappointed
items.meaning: very sad because something was not as good as you hoped
items.example: We were **bitterly disappointed** when the match was called off because of the rain.
more: The final score was **bitterly disappointing** for the home fans.
Tom was **bitterly disappointed** with his driving test result.
items.watchOut: «Сильно розчарований» — bitterly або deeply disappointed, а не strongly. Disappointed — про людину (я розчарований), disappointing — про річ (розчаровує).

items.pattern: bitterly / deeply regret sth / -ing / that…
items.meaning: feel very sorry about something you did or didn't do
items.example: I **bitterly regret** not visiting my grandmother more often.
more: She **deeply regrets** selling her old piano.
You'll **bitterly regret** it if you don't take this chance.
items.watchOut: «Дуже шкодую» — I bitterly / deeply regret it, а не strongly regret. Після regret — -ing або that: regret saying it.

items.pattern: bitterly resent sth / -ing / the fact that… · also deeply resent
items.meaning: feel angry and unhappy because something seems unfair
items.example: She **bitterly resented** having to work every weekend while her colleagues stayed at home.
more: My brother still **bitterly resents** the fact that I got the bigger bedroom.
Many locals **bitterly resent** the new parking charges.
items.watchOut: Resent — ображатися, обурюватися, а не «надіслати знову» (re-send). Вимова з [z]. Після resent — -ing або the fact that.

items.pattern: complain bitterly (about sth) · bitterly criticise sb / sth
items.meaning: complain about or criticise something in a very angry, unhappy way
items.example: The passengers **complained bitterly** about the two-hour delay.
more: My grandad **complains bitterly** every time bus fares go up.
The new menu was **bitterly criticised** by regular customers.
items.watchOut: Скаржитися на щось — complain about sth (не complain on), комусь — complain to sb. Bitterly зазвичай стоїть після complain.

items.pattern: cry / weep bitterly
items.meaning: cry a lot because you are very sad
items.example: The little girl **cried bitterly** when her balloon flew away.
more: He **wept bitterly** at his best friend's funeral.
She sat on the stairs and **cried bitterly** for an hour.
items.watchOut: Гірко плакати — cry bitterly: тут калька працює. А «сильно плакала» — не cried strongly, а cried hard або cried her eyes out. Weep — книжніше за cry.

items.pattern: deeply ashamed (of sth / of yourself / that…)
items.meaning: feeling very bad about something wrong you did
items.example: I'm **deeply ashamed** of the way I spoke to my mum yesterday.
more: He was **deeply ashamed** that he'd forgotten his daughter's birthday.
You should be **deeply ashamed** of yourself!
items.watchOut: «Мені соромно» — I'm ashamed (of sth), а не It's shame for me. Ashamed — сором через поганий вчинок; embarrassed — ніяково.

items.pattern: deeply concerned (about sth / that…)
items.meaning: very worried about something important
items.example: The doctor was **deeply concerned** about my grandad's blood pressure.
more: Residents are **deeply concerned** about the lorries on our narrow street.
I'm **deeply concerned** that the kids spend so much time indoors.
items.watchOut: Стурбований чимось — concerned about sth. Concerned with — «стосується»: The book is concerned with family life. Deeply concerned трохи офіційніше за really worried.

items.pattern: deeply shocked (by sth / to hear…)
items.meaning: very surprised and upset
items.example: We were all **deeply shocked** by the news of the accident.
more: I was **deeply shocked** to hear that the old cinema was closing.
My parents were **deeply shocked** by how much the town had changed.
items.watchOut: Не strongly shocked. Офіційніше — deeply shocked, у розмові часто absolutely shocked.

items.pattern: deeply committed to sth / sb / -ing
items.meaning: giving a lot of time and energy to something or someone you believe in
items.example: She's **deeply committed** to her work at the animal shelter.
more: They're still **deeply committed** to each other after forty years of marriage.
He's **deeply committed** to his family and never works at weekends.
items.watchOut: Відданий чомусь — committed to sth / to doing sth: committed to helping, а не committed to help чи committed for.

items.pattern: deeply moved (by sth) · deeply affected (by sth)
items.meaning: feeling strong emotions, often sadness or sympathy, because of something
items.example: The whole family was **deeply moved** by Grandma's speech at her ninetieth birthday party.
more: Many people were **deeply affected** by the film about refugees.
I was **deeply moved** by the letters my grandad wrote during the war.
items.watchOut: Moved тут — зворушений, а не «переїхав». Глибоко вдячний — deeply grateful: українське «глибоко» тут теж = deeply.

items.pattern: deeply hurt (by sth / that…) · about feelings
items.meaning: very upset because someone was unkind to you
items.example: She was **deeply hurt** that none of her friends remembered her birthday.
more: I was **deeply hurt** by what my brother said at dinner.
He felt **deeply hurt** when everyone laughed at his idea.
items.watchOut: Deeply hurt — про почуття. Про тілесну травму кажуть badly hurt / seriously hurt: He was badly hurt in the accident.

items.pattern: care deeply about sth / sb · also deeply care about
items.meaning: think something or someone is very important to you
items.example: My parents **care deeply about** what we eat.
more: She **cares deeply about** her garden and talks to her tomatoes.
Good teachers **care deeply about** their students.
items.watchOut: Care about — бути небайдужим, перейматися; care for — доглядати (care for an elderly parent).

items.pattern: deeply religious · a deeply religious family / person
items.meaning: with very strong religious beliefs
items.example: My grandmother was **deeply religious** and went to church every Sunday.
more: They come from a **deeply religious** family.
He isn't **deeply religious**, but he loves the quiet of old churches.
items.watchOut: Віруючий — religious або a believer, а не believing.

items.pattern: deeply unhappy (about / with sth)
items.meaning: very sad, or not at all satisfied, often for a long time
items.example: He was **deeply unhappy** in his job, so he finally left.
more: Parents are **deeply unhappy** about the new school timetable.
She seemed **deeply unhappy** in the months after the move.
items.watchOut: Unhappy — і нещасний, і незадоволений: unhappy with the service / about the changes.

items.pattern: ridiculously cheap / expensive
items.meaning: so cheap or so expensive that it's hard to believe
items.example: The jeans were **ridiculously cheap** in the sale, so I bought two pairs.
more: Coffee at the airport is always **ridiculously expensive**.
We stayed in a **ridiculously cheap** guesthouse by the sea.
items.watchOut: «Смішна ціна», «за смішні гроші» — ridiculously cheap, a ridiculously low price. Не funnily cheap і не a funny price.

items.pattern: ridiculously easy (to do sth)
items.meaning: much easier than you expected
items.example: The recipe is **ridiculously easy**: you just mix everything and bake it.
more: The first level of the game was **ridiculously easy**.
Putting up the new shelves was **ridiculously easy**.

items.pattern: ridiculously high / low · prices, rent, pay, numbers
items.meaning: far too high or far too low
items.example: House prices in our town are **ridiculously high**.
more: My first salary was **ridiculously low**.
Petrol prices are **ridiculously high** at motorway service stations.
items.watchOut: Про ціни, зарплату, оренду — high / low, а не big / small: a ridiculously high rent, а не a big rent.

items.pattern: ridiculously early · get up / start / close ridiculously early
items.meaning: much earlier than is normal or comfortable
items.uk: до смішного рано, ні світ ні зоря
items.example: My grandad gets up **ridiculously early**, even on holiday.
more: The shops close **ridiculously early** in this town: five o'clock on a Saturday!
We got to the party **ridiculously early** and helped blow up the balloons.

items.pattern: ridiculously small / large
items.meaning: far too small or far too big
items.example: The portions in that restaurant are **ridiculously small**.
more: Our first flat had a **ridiculously small** kitchen.
He ordered a **ridiculously large** pizza and couldn't eat half of it.
items.watchOut: Large — трохи офіційніше за big; так кажуть про розміри одягу, порцій, кави: a large coffee.

items.pattern: ridiculously long / short
items.meaning: far too long or far too short
items.example: There was a **ridiculously long** queue at the post office.
more: The summer holidays always feel **ridiculously short**.
The film was **ridiculously long**: nearly four hours.
items.watchOut: Довга черга — a long queue, а не a big queue.

items.pattern: strongly recommend / suggest that… / -ing · strongly recommend sth
items.meaning: advise someone very firmly to do something
items.example: I **strongly recommend** that you book a table: it's always full on Fridays.
more: The doctor **strongly suggested** that I take a few days off.
Warm clothes are **strongly recommended** for the boat trip.
items.watchOut: Suggest / recommend + that або -ing: I strongly suggest that you leave early / I suggest leaving early. Не I suggest you to leave.

items.phrase: strongly oppose / be strongly opposed to
items.pattern: strongly oppose sth · be strongly opposed to sth / -ing
items.meaning: disagree with a plan or an idea very firmly and want to stop it
items.example: My grandparents **strongly oppose** the idea of moving into a smaller flat.
more: The farmers **strongly opposed** the new road across their fields.
I'm **strongly opposed to** children having phones at primary school.
items.watchOut: Oppose sth — без прийменника; be opposed to sth. Не oppose against і не opposed against. Можна і strongly, і utterly opposed.

items.pattern: strongly believe (that…) · feel strongly about sth
items.meaning: be very sure that your opinion is right
items.example: I **strongly believe** that children should learn to swim at school.
more: My dad **feels strongly** about people dropping litter.
She **strongly believes** that breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
items.watchOut: Feel strongly about sth — мати тверду думку щодо чогось (strongly після feel). Але «дуже сподіваюся» — не strongly hope, а I really / sincerely hope.

items.pattern: strongly deny sth / -ing / that…
items.meaning: say very firmly that something is not true
items.example: My son **strongly denied** eating the last piece of cake, but he had chocolate all over his face.
more: The shop **strongly denies** selling out-of-date food.
She **strongly denied** that she had broken the vase.
items.watchOut: Deny + -ing або that: deny eating it / deny that he ate it. Не deny to eat.

items.pattern: strongly support sth / sb
items.meaning: agree with something or someone and want it to succeed
items.example: Most people in our street **strongly support** the idea of a new playground.
more: My parents **strongly supported** my decision to study abroad.
The plan to plant more trees is **strongly supported** by local residents.
items.watchOut: Підтримувати ідею, людину — support. Maintain — підтримувати стан: maintain the temperature, maintain the garden.

items.pattern: strongly condemn sth
items.meaning: say publicly and firmly that something is very wrong
items.example: The mayor **strongly condemned** the violence after the football match.
more: Animal lovers **strongly condemned** the cruel treatment of the horses.
The football club **strongly condemns** any racist chanting.
items.watchOut: Вимова: n у кінці condemn не звучить.

items.pattern: strongly object to sth / -ing
items.meaning: say firmly that you don't agree with or don't like something
items.uk: рішуче заперечувати проти, бути категорично проти
items.example: Many drivers **strongly object to** the new speed cameras.
more: Neighbours **strongly objected to** the noise from the new bar.
My mum **strongly objects to** us eating in front of the TV.
items.watchOut: Object to sth / to doing sth: object to paying, а не object to pay і не object against. Дієслово object — наголос на другий склад: /əbˈdʒekt/.

items.pattern: strongly influence sth / sb · be strongly influenced by
items.meaning: have a big effect on what someone does or thinks
items.example: My grandfather **strongly influenced** my love of gardening.
more: Where you live **strongly influences** how you travel to work.
Teenagers are **strongly influenced** by their friends.
items.watchOut: Influence як дієслово — без прийменника: influence her choice. Іменник — have an influence on sth. Не influence on her choice.

items.pattern: argue strongly that… / for / against sth
items.meaning: give firm reasons for an opinion
items.example: My sister **argued strongly** that we should all go on holiday together.
more: Some parents **argue strongly** for a later start to the school day.
He **argued strongly** against buying a new car.
items.watchOut: Argue — і «сваритися», і «доводити, обстоювати думку». Argue strongly for / against sth — переконливо виступати за / проти; argue with sb — сваритися з кимось.

warmup.uk: Дуже малоймовірно, що я закінчу ремонт до літа.
warmup.q: It's ___ unlikely that I'll finish decorating the flat before the summer.
warmup.explain: З likely / unlikely кажуть highly. Strongly — з дієсловами думки, utterly — з «крайніми» словами.
Highly recommended — дуже хвалять, радять. Ще можна strongly recommended, але не extremely.
Ridiculous — «крайнє» слово, тому utterly або absolutely ridiculous.
Absolutely — з «крайніми» словами: absolutely exhausted. Але very tired, а не absolutely tired.

warmup.uk: Я був страшенно розчарований, коли мене не взяли на роботу.
warmup.q: I was ___ disappointed when I didn't get the job.
warmup.explain: «Сильно розчарований» — bitterly або deeply disappointed, не strongly.

warmup.uk: Мені глибоко соромно за свої слова.
warmup.q: I'm ___ ashamed of what I said.
warmup.explain: Глибоко соромно — deeply ashamed: тут калька з української працює.
«Смішно дешево», «за смішні гроші» — ridiculously cheap. Funnily означає «кумедно».

warmup.uk: Я категорично проти того, щоб платити за пакети.
warmup.q: I ___ object to paying for plastic bags.
warmup.explain: Бути категорично проти — strongly object to sth / to doing sth.

A.q: It's ___ unlikely that the shop will still be open at this time.
A.explain: З likely / unlikely кажуть highly (або very). Strongly — з дієсловами думки, utterly — з «крайніми» словами.

A.q: These new tablets are highly ___: my headache went in ten minutes.
A.explain: Effective — дієвий. Competitive (з великою конкуренцією) і controversial (суперечливий) до ліків тут не пасують.

A.q: The new statue in the town square is ___ controversial.
A.explain: Highly зазвичай іде з позитивними словами, але highly controversial — виняток.

B.q: Waiting two hours for a pizza is ___ ridiculous!
B.explain: Ridiculous — «крайнє» слово: utterly або absolutely ridiculous, не highly і не strongly.

B.q: After the marathon I was absolutely ___.
B.explain: Absolutely — з «крайніми» словами: exhausted. Tired і sleepy — звичайні, з ними кажуть very.

B.q: My uncle is absolutely convinced ___ the benefits of cold showers.
B.explain: Переконаний у чомусь — convinced of sth, не convinced in.

C.q: I ___ regret not learning to swim as a child.
C.explain: «Дуже шкодую» — bitterly або deeply regret, не strongly.

C.q: The rent is ridiculously ___ for such a small flat.
C.explain: Про ціни й оренду — high / low, не big. Tall — про зріст.

C.q: My mum is strongly opposed ___ us getting a motorbike.
C.explain: Be opposed to sth: після opposed — to, не against.

practice.q: The match is ___ unlikely to start on time: the pitch is still covered in snow.
If you leave your bike unlocked here, it's ___ likely to get stolen.
My brother's ___ unlikely to call before noon: he never gets up before eleven.
It's ___ unusual to see a fox in the city centre in the middle of the day.
For a cat to live to twenty-five is highly ___.
My cousin's clothes shop has been ___ successful: she now employs ten people.
The charity concert was ___ successful and raised enough to repair the church roof.
The car wash on the corner is ___ profitable: there's a queue every weekend.
Their ice-cream van is highly ___ in summer but loses money in winter.
There are 300 applicants for every place, so getting into that drama school is highly ___.
My sister is highly ___ and hates losing, even at cards.
Cool running water is a ___ effective way to stop a burn from getting worse.

example.title: Rain at the lake
example.uk:
Минулого літа ми поїхали з наметами до озера. Кемпінг нам дуже радили, і він був до смішного дешевий, тож ми одразу його забронювали.

Першої ж ночі почався дощ, і він не припинявся три дні. Намет протікав, діти були зовсім нещасні, а чоловік гірко скаржився на все підряд. До вівторка ми всі геть виснажилися.

Аж тут власниця прийшла до нашого намету з гарячим супом і сухими ковдрами. Ми були глибоко зворушені. Вона розповіла, що стільки дощу в липні — для цих місць украй незвично.

Ми поїхали на день раніше, гірко розчаровані, але я твердо вірю, що ми ще повернемося. Щоправда, наступного разу я спершу перевірю прогноз погоди.
example.en:
Last summer we went camping by a lake. The campsite came [[highly recommended|a8]] and was [[ridiculously cheap|c15]], so we booked it straight away.

On the first night it started to rain, and it didn't stop for three days. The tent leaked, the kids were [[utterly miserable|b9]] and my husband [[complained bitterly|c4]] about everything. By Tuesday we were all [[absolutely exhausted|b10]].

Then the owner came to our tent with hot soup and dry blankets. We were [[deeply moved|c10]]. She told us that so much rain in July was [[highly unusual|a2]] there.

We left a day early, [[bitterly disappointed|c1]], but I [[strongly believe|c23]] we'll go back. Next time, though, I'll check the forecast first.
